screens.prompt: In B8, return the name of the rep with the highest score from A2:B7, ranking the table with SORT before you pick a cell.

hints.syntax: =INDEX(SORT(A2:B7,2,-1),1,1): SORT builds the ranked block, INDEX picks one cell from it.
hints.func-sort: Sorting is the point of this lesson. Reading the answer off the screen does not survive next month's update.
hints.func-index: SORT returns a whole block of rows. INDEX is how you ask that block for its first row and first column.
hints.require-ref: Point SORT at the table starting at row 2 so the check can see the scores column.
hints.value: The cell you picked is not the top of the ranking. Check the sort order and which row of the sorted block you asked for.
hints.error: #VALUE! here means the sort index is outside the table width, or INDEX was given one argument instead of a row and a column.

reject.why: ranks the table correctly but returns the whole block, so the answer cell holds a spilled range instead of one name
sorts ascending, so the first row is the lowest score
sorts by the rep name instead of the score
picks the second row of the ranking, not the first
hard-codes the row Mia happens to sit on today
returns the score 95 rather than the name attached to it
the sort index is outside the two-column table, so SORT reports #VALUE!
starts below the table and never looks at the scores column from row 2

docs.explain: SORT returns a new block of rows in the order you ask for without touching the source table. The second argument names the column to sort on, so 2 means the score column, and the third argument takes 1 for ascending or -1 for descending. Six reps sit in rows 2 to 7 with scores of 88, 95, 72, 91, 61 and 80. Sorting on column 2 descending puts Mia's 95 on the first row, Ivy's 91 on the second and Sam's 61 last. SORT on its own spills that whole ranked block, and a block is not a single answer. INDEX pulls one cell out of it: row 1, column 1 is the name at the top. That two-step shape is the reusable pattern, because changing row 1 to row 2 gives the runner-up without a second formula. Two limits bite in practice. The sort index counts columns inside the array, not columns on the sheet, so 3 on a two-column table returns #VALUE!. The spill also needs empty cells below it, or Excel reports #SPILL!.

errors.text: The sort index is larger than the array is wide, or INDEX was given a row but no column.
The ranked block has nowhere to land because a cell below the formula is already occupied.
The sort index points at a column the array does not have.
The workbook predates dynamic arrays, so SORT is not recognised at all.

docs.atWork: Top customer, worst-performing line, latest invoice: ranking a small table and reading one cell is a daily question that a filter cannot answer.
docs.outcome: Rank a table with a formula and pull one cell out of the ranked block.

seo.title: SORT in Excel, then INDEX one cell out
seo.description: SORT ranks a block in the order you ask for without touching the source. INDEX then pulls one cell, so row 1 is the top and row 2 the runner-up.
